_comment: Per-project harness config. Copy to your project root as hydra-agents.json and edit. All paths are relative to the project root (checked in, portable). This example carries Hydra's own values.
_sessionPrefix_comment: Optional. Machine-global prefix for tmux session / agent names, so two projects on one host don't collide on `staging` / `feature_NNN_*`. Defaults to the repo name from issueRepo + '-' (here: 'hydra-'). Override only if the repo name is awkward. Branch/worktree names stay unprefixed.
_standardizedBranches_comment: Optional. Space-separated set of branch names that exist on EVERY machine (staging, …) and so must be machine-qualified in the session/agent name to stay distinct across a multi-machine fleet — e.g. staging -> 'hydra-staging-<machine1>' / 'hydra-staging-<machine2>' (suffix from `hostname -s`). Issue branches (feature_NNN_*) are already unique and stay unqualified. Defaults to 'staging'.
_stagingPeers_comment: Optional. The exact session names of this project's staging sessions on OTHER machines: the only off-machine recipients a staging session may message (docs/cross-worktree-messages.md § Project isolation). Use the name other machines resolve, which is the Remote Control label; claude-remote launches use the same string for both. Never fill this from a ListAgents listing. Example values are placeholders.
_listAgents_comment: Optional, "ask" (default) or "deny": what the peer-scope hook (bin/claude-hooks/peer-scope.sh) does with ListAgents, the account-wide session listing that shows every project. Agents address their own project's peers by computed name, so they never need it.
_opaqueNames_comment: Optional, default false: true names sessions, Remote Control labels, tmux and terminal titles p-<hash> instead of <prefix><branch>. Projects are kept apart by scoped messaging, not by names, so leave this off unless the names themselves must not be seen.
_visibility_comment: Optional: "public" or "private". Decides isolation per repo (docs/cross-worktree-messages.md § Project isolation). If absent, the harness asks `gh repo view`; if that can't tell, it treats the repo as private (fail closed). A private repo must check in its guard (bin/project-guard; docs/private-projects.md).
_privateInbound_comment: Optional, "accept" (default), "hold" or "refuse": how guarded sessions (private repo, or sensitive machine) treat inbound cross-session messages. The guard gates outgoing sends, so inbound is normally accepted; with Claude Code it is set at launch (--settings), the only scope where accept applies.
_machineLocal_comment: Machine-local settings go in hydra-agents.local.json beside this file (gitignored), never here: machineSensitivity ("sensitive" | "open"; default "open" where ~/.hydra-sandbox exists, else "sensitive"), sensitivePaths (extra ~-relative paths to keep agents out of), sandboxBash ("true" to turn on Claude Code's Bash sandbox there). Any optional field set in the local file overrides this one.
